name: Greater Indonesia
summary: Greater Indonesia (Indonesia Raya; in its Malay form Melayu Raya) is the idea of one independent state uniting the Dutch East Indies with British Malaya and, in some versions, North Borneo and Timor, on the ground of shared Malay history and culture and against the colonial partition. It arose in the 1930s and 1940s among Malay nationalists such as Ibrahim Yaacob and Burhanuddin al-Helmy and in Indonesia's 1945 independence committee, where Yamin and Sukarno argued for borders wider than the Dutch East Indies. It is a territorial and national-unity programme, and the sources record little on economic, social or constitutional questions.
scope: The pan-Malay and pan-archipelago union idea of c. 1930s-1960s: the KMM and PKMM Melayu Raya strand (Ibrahim Yaacob, Burhanuddin al-Helmy), the 1945 BPUPK territorial debate (Muhammad Yamin, Sukarno), and the later opposition to Malaysia as it bears on the idea. Positions of those leaders on matters unrelated to the union (religion, economy, constitutional form) are not treated as the idea's own.
